title: Volume 1 Chapter 1 — The Garden of Women
content: Sitting on a bench inside the cargo hold of the transport aircraft with my seatbelt securely fastened, I looked down at my brand-new military uniform.
The rank insignia pinned to my chest was that of a Warrant Officer.
I, who had spent my entire time running through the dirt of the front lines as a mere Corporal, had somehow risen to the status of an officer cadet in the span of just half a year.
If my old platoon leader were here right now, he would undoubtedly give me a mock salute with a massive grin on his face just to tease me.
If MC were still alive, he would probably laugh it off as a terrible joke.
And Comic would have been thrilled, claiming it was the perfect material for his next story.
But within the cargo hold, echoing with the deafening, monotonous roar of the aircraft's engines, I was completely alone.

Having narrowly endured the agonizing surgical operations and the grueling months of rehabilitation that followed, the day had finally arrived for me to be stationed at the base that would serve as the testing ground for our project.
Glancing down at my right hand, which was covered in a black leather glove, I clenched and opened my fingers a few times to confirm the sensation.
The condition of my left leg wasn't bad either.
A faint trace of artificiality still lingered when I moved, but functionally, it was working without a single hitch.
The various internal organs I had lost—most notably my heart—were also operating perfectly.
Even the vision in my left eye, which had been completely blinded during the ambush, was now entirely indistinguishable from its original state.

Part of me found it hard to believe that my body had truly undergone regenerative treatments using cells harvested from an actual Gijuu, but the excruciating, unforgettable pain I experienced during the operations and recovery was the ultimate proof.
"No matter what kind of experiment lies ahead, I will endure it and see it through to the end."
As I muttered those words aloud to steady my resolve, the pilot's voice boomed loudly through the overhead speaker from the cockpit.
『We are arriving. Prepare to disembark.』
"Understood."
Even though I knew my voice wouldn't carry back to him over the engine noise, I gave a firm reply and checked my meager belongings.
Since I owned very little in this world, everything to my name fit easily inside a single boston bag.
Stepping out of the transport aircraft, the intense, blinding glare of the afternoon sun momentarily forced me to squint.
As my eyes adjusted to the light, the surrounding scenery made me instantly doubt my own senses.
Instead of the rugged, mud-caked forward outposts or the heavily fortified, gray concrete bunkers I was accustomed to on the front lines, I was looking at a pristine landscape.
Beautifully paved walkways wound between vast, manicured green lawns, and elegant white buildings stood neatly beneath the clear blue sky.
It bore absolutely no resemblance to a military installation; it looked exactly like an elite, high-class academy campus.
This was the Third Academy—the specialized training facility and strategic stronghold where humanity's ultimate weapons, the Valkyries, were raised and stationed.
As I made my way down the path, I caught sight of young girls walking around in small groups. Some wore immaculate school uniforms, while others were clad in athletic training gear.
Because only females possessed the specific biological aptitude required to generate the forcefields necessary to operate a Valkyrie Dress, every single student enrolled here was a young woman.
Dressed in my crisp military uniform and carrying my solitary bag, I realized with absolute certainty that I was a complete anomaly in this environment—the only male on the entire campus.
Meanwhile, inside one of the campus buildings, the classrooms were filled with the lively chatter of students after morning arrival.
In the classroom designated for Class 5, a silver-haired girl named Louise Durand was enthusiastically speaking with her classmates.
With her long, softly waved silver hair, beautifully refined features, and a naturally gentle countenance, Louise exuded a remarkably serene aura.
Despite being born overseas, she spoke fluent, flawless Japanese through sheer personal dedication.
However, her hard work had also left her with a peculiar habit of eagerly sharing random trivia with her peers first thing in the morning.

"Hey, did you guys know? People usually think the word 'unprecedented' means doing something completely reckless and chaotic. But it actually means achieving something that absolutely no one else in history has ever managed to accomplish before! It's an incredibly misunderstood phrase!"
Hearing Louise eagerly dish out her trivia, Asai Mami let out a quiet, exasperated sigh.
Mami, an eighteen-year-old with sharp eyes and a short navy blue bob, was older than Louise and carried an air of cool aloofness that made her somewhat unapproachable to others.
She was the type of person who firmly believed in keeping her personal interactions with fellow classmates to an absolute minimum.
After all, the candidates placed in Class 5 were technically rivals, all desperately competing for the same limited scouting spots to become official Valkyries.
While most girls avoided unnecessary mingling, Mami found herself lowering her guard around Louise, consistently tolerating her quirks even if she acted textually bored by them.
"Where on earth do you even dig up these random facts?" Mami asked with a dry expression.
"The internet!" Louise replied brightly.
"...Well, regardless, it's not like people actually use the word 'unprecedented' all that often in daily conversation anyway."
"Huh?! Really?!" Louise slumped slightly, looking visibly shocked that her hard-earned trivia wasn't more practical.
Seeing Louise's dramatic reaction, a couple of her other classmates laughed softly before shifting the conversation to a much more serious topic.
"I heard you were officially placed on the scout candidate list, Louise. That's amazing! But... I also heard that Lieutenant Hayase was looking at you earlier, and she didn't look happy at all."
Louise's bright expression faltered, replaced by a look of deep worry.
"Yeah... I don't know what I did wrong. Personally, I don't have any hard feelings toward her, but it really seems like Lieutenant Hayase... completely despises me."
The two girls gave Louise deeply sympathetic looks.
"To think a classmate you used to know back in middle school is now the ultimate Ace... and out of all people, to be hated by *that* Hayase. Talk about terrible luck."
"Seriously, getting on the bad side of the academy's absolute strongest Valkyrie... I feel so sorry for you, Louise."
For the students in Class 5, who were treated strictly as a reserve force, earning the animosity of an elite Ace was a devastating disadvantage.
Among the entire student body, Hayase Maya was widely recognized as the single most powerful Valkyrie at the Third Academy when it came to pure individual combat proficiency.
In fact, even the instructors and high-ranking faculty members treated Maya with a distinct level of exceptionalism.
Her only notable flaw was her absolute isolation; she flatly refused to allow any partners or attendants to stand by her side, choosing to fight completely alone on the battlefield.
To some, she was a majestic, independent figure. To others, she was completely isolated and lonely.
Because of her fiercely aggressive and relentless fighting style, she was frequently referred to by the hushed nickname of the 'Female Warrior' behind her back.
The two classmates offered a mix of pity and dark humor as they continued to tease her.
"At this rate, it looks like your school life is going to be cut short before it even truly begins."
Louise looked like she was on the verge of tears.
"Don't say that! Trust me, I already know exactly how bad of a situation I'm in right now!"
Meanwhile, a short distance away along the academy pathways, Hayase Maya was walking briskly.
She had just passed near the area where the Class 5 girls were gathered, deliberately projecting an intense, suffocating pressure that left them thoroughly intimidated.
Another female student, Sorajima Mai, quickly caught up to her side.
Mai kept her eyes fixed straight ahead, not even glancing back as she questioned her companion's hostile behavior.
"What was the point of going out of your way to intimidate those Class 5 girls just now? That doesn't seem like you at all, Maya."
